what_it_does: Some recent chip designs embed small arithmetic units directly inside the cache — the fast on-chip memory that normally just stores data — so that certain computations can run without moving data to a separate math unit. Earlier designs committed entire cache arrays to this compute role, leaving most of those arrays sitting idle because real workloads do not need full-time computing capacity, and the remaining pure-storage arrays got overwhelmed during bursts of memory access. MagiCache makes the assignment flexible at the level of individual cache rows: any row in any array can be switched dynamically between being a storage line and being a compute line, based on what the workload needs right now, with negligible extra hardware. A software-visible 'virtual engine' monitors the current balance of compute versus storage demand and reassigns rows on the fly. It also overlaps the latency of fetching new data from large, slow off-chip memory chips with ongoing arithmetic, so neither resource sits waiting for the other.
